To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) an effective DA method is not only about distribution alignment, but also about discriminative learning and geometry-aware learning; 2) the discriminative learning and the geometry-aware learning are complementary to each other; 3) the proposed DA method is able to achieve state of the art performance in a wide range of DA problems; 4) the proposed DA model is able to learn discriminative and geometry-aware features for DA.

we propose a new DA method, DGA-DA which implements jointly the discriminative and geometry aware DA, and that DGA-DA outperforms the state of the art in 36 image classification tasks over 6 benchmarks.

the proposed method is able to effectively adapt source domain to the target domain in terms of both data distribution alignment as well as data discriminativeness.
